title: Geometric irreducibility can be tested on finite separable extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $R$ a commutative $k$-algebra, meaning a commutative ring equipped with a homomorphism $k\to R$. Form tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with multiplication $(r\otimes a)(s\otimes b)=rs\otimes ab$ and unit $1\otimes1$. The following are equivalent: (1) for every field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kL)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]; (2) for every finite separable algebraic field extension $E/k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kE)$ is irreducible. Here finite means finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and irreducible includes nonempty. No finite-generation or reducedness assumption on $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: Condition (1) implies (2): each finite separable extension is in particular a field extension, so specialize the quantifier in (1).

Use Mathlib tensor-product algebra maps, symmetry, congruence and cancelBaseChange for the scalar identifications. Tensoring a field-linear injection with a vector space is injective by Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap or Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap. These supply all scalar-map injections directly; no ideal-contraction lemma is needed. The finite test quantifies over Type (max u v w), so transport it to fields in Type u using ULift.algEquiv and TensorProduct.congr.

source.place: Tag 037K proof, scalar-extension maps; tensor bilinearity and faithful-flat injectivity replace the minimal-prime going-down argument.

proof.text: Choose Mathlib SeparableClosure k. The test at E=k gives a nonempty prime spectrum of R tensor k, hence that tensor ring and R are nontrivial. The separable closure is a nonzero vector space over k and therefore faithfully flat; Mathlib faithful-flat tensor nontriviality makes R tensor SeparableClosure k nontrivial. Thus its nilradical is proper, using Ideal.radical_eq_top.

source.place: Tag 037K, (2) implies (3), including nonemptiness of the spectrum.

proof.text: For x,y in R tensor SeparableClosure k, apply Mathlib exists_fg_and_mem_baseChange to each and take the supremum D of the resulting finitely generated coefficient subalgebras. Algebra.IsAlgebraic.toIntermediateField makes D an intermediate field E without changing its underlying algebra. It is finite-dimensional by Algebra.IsIntegral.finite, and separable as a subextension of the separable closure. Tensor-map composition lifts x,y to xE,yE in R tensor E. The map to R tensor SeparableClosure k is injective by flatness over k, so nilpotence of xy implies nilpotence of xE*yE. The test at E makes its nilradical prime; hence xE or yE is nilpotent. Mapping that nilpotence equation back proves x or y nilpotent. Thus the proper nilradical of R tensor SeparableClosure k is prime and its spectrum is irreducible.

source.place: Tag 037K, (2) implies (3): the finite-subextension argument, expressed using the nilradical criterion Tag 00ES instead of minimal primes.

proof.text: Apply Field.exists_common_extension over k to SeparableClosure k and the arbitrary test field L, obtaining compatible embeddings i and j into M. Use i to give M its SeparableClosure k-algebra structure and scalar tower. The spectrum of M is irreducible because M is a field. Tensor symmetry identifies the irreducible spectrum from the previous step with that of SeparableClosure k tensor R. Apply IsSepClosed.irreducibleSpace_tensorProduct over SeparableClosure k to M and SeparableClosure k tensor R. TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange identifies the resulting tensor ring with M tensor R, proving its spectrum irreducible.

source.place: Tag 037K, final proof paragraph; Tag 00I7, lemma-separably-closed-irreducible, applied directly over the separable closure.

proof.text: The map TensorProduct.map j (AlgHom.id k R) from L tensor R to M tensor R is injective by Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap. For an injective unital ring map f, nilpotence of f(x) is equivalent to nilpotence of x, by map_pow and injectivity. Thus the source nilradical equals the comap of the target nilradical. A comap of a prime ideal is prime, so the nilradical criterion descends irreducibility to L tensor R. Tensor symmetry gives the required spectrum of R tensor L. This proves the reverse implication for every L.

source.place: Tag 037K, final descent from a common overfield, via contraction of the nilradical along the injective scalar-extension map.

proof_origin.place: Tag 037K, finite-separable tests imply the separable-closure test, followed by the common-overfield argument and Tag 00I7 over that separable closure. The Lean proof implements finite coefficient support via Mathlib finitely generated subalgebras, promotes the algebraic coefficient subalgebra to an intermediate field, and uses flatness over a field for tensor-map injectivity; it does not use ideal contraction.
